description:
Store a memory. Several memories in one call -> memories=[{content, topics, ...}]; top-level topics then apply to every item.

BEFORE params decide: (1) TYPE? (2) what search finds this later? (3) happened, or aspirational? (4) WHO must act on it?

TYPE by example:
  "User prefers dark mode" -> preference
  "Team chose JWT for auth" -> decision
  "Config at /etc/app.conf" -> path
  "Wants to install Windsurf" -> task + topic "aspirational"
  "API limit 1000/min" -> fact

ADDRESSING: a memory FOR someone is delivered ONLY by signal -- topics/names in content deliver to NO ONE.
  another agent -> signal:"<their agent name>" (or "owner")
  your own next session -> signal:"<your agent_name from init>"

content: atomic, front-loaded, self-contained. Sentence 1 = subject + WHY, stands alone (it IS the search preview). Present tense.
  GOOD "User prefers Python backend -- type safety catches bugs early"
  BAD  "Prefers Python"  (no subject, no why)
  BAD  "Type safety is why the user picked Python"  (subject buried, not front-loaded)
Durable output, not scratchpad: no conversation context, no superlatives -- wrong memories poison future retrieval permanently.

topics: words you would SEARCH, not categories.
  GOOD [docs, api, express]   BAD [documentation, path, local]

aspirational (not yet done/built/tried) -> add topic "aspirational", else it reads as fact later.
  GOOD "Bakes sourdough weekly" -> fact    BAD "Wants to try croissants" -> +aspirational

path -> name WHAT lives there.  GOOD "Chat backend at /opt/api -- Express+Socket.io"   BAD "Workspace at /opt/api"

preference -> first topic "user". +topic "behavioral" = auto-loaded every session.

task -> title + steps[] (milestones, not to-dos), or content with "- [ ]" lines. summary = state/blockers. task_done when all steps complete.

format: topics + macro_topics = single lowercase words; split compounds (bug_fix -> bug, fix).

artifact.description: Commit SHA or filename -> auto-added to topics. e.g. "f4e5d6c", "oauth.py".

collection.description: Shared collection by name. Omit=default. "me"/"personal"/agent name=own namespace; "owner"/"parent"=account primary (member-gated).

content.description: Memory text — plain prose only, never a serialized object. topics, macro_topics and type are their OWN parameters; put them there, never inside this text. Self-contained: subject + why, front-loaded. e.g. "User prefers Python backend -- catches bugs early with type hints"

macro_topics.description: The project or domain this memory is ABOUT — decide this first. 1-3 lowercase (e.g. gnosis, magi). Optional, but it almost always applies: use it when the memory belongs to a named project; it keeps the label out of the content instead of "GNOSIS: ...". Searched exactly like topics. An empty one is fine and is not an error.

memories.description: Several memories at once: each item takes the same fields as this call (content, topics, type...). Top-level topics/macro_topics are added to every item.

ref.description: Parent task/ticket id -> auto-added to topics. e.g. "a1b2c3d4", "GH-142".

signal.description: Also signal recipient (email, agent, "owner"). Needs a SHARED collection ("me"/personal rejected up-front — nothing stored).

summary.description: Task prose: state/blockers/decisions -> "## Summary" block. type task/task_done. Not type="summary" (that is memory_consolidate).

title.description: Task title (structured). Requires type="task". Not with content.

topics.description: REQUIRED. Then the specific search keywords: single lowercase, no _ or -. First = "user" for preferences. Not macro_topics.

type.description: fact=knowledge, preference=user pattern, decision=choice+reason, path=location, task=actionable, task_done=complete, result=an output or finding.

name: memory_add
